newsitem.title: USA: Trial delayed for former Stephens banker Bynum.
newsitem.headline: Trial delayed for former Stephens banker Bynum.

text.p: The perjury trial of former Arkansas investment banker Preston Bynum has been delayed indefinitely, a court clerk said Thursday.

Bynum's trial had been scheduled to begin on Aug. 4 in U.S. District Court in Pensacola. It was postponed at the request of Bynum's attorney, Jack Lassiter, who could not be reached for comment. A new trial date has not been set.

Bynum resigned from the Little Rock, Ark., firm Stephans Inc after pleading guilty in 1995 to a bribery charge. He admitted he paid Terry Busbee, a former commissioner with the Escambia County Utility Authority, $67,200 in loans and cash to steer municipal bond underwriting business to the firm.

Bynum was subsequently charged with perjury in an indictment unsealed in March. The indictment alleges he lied to a grand jury when he said that he thought the money would be used to pay a consultant.
The indictment alleges Bynum knew the money was for Busbee.
